what the data shows: Runs off the bat per innings went from 147 (2008) to 157 (2019). Sixes per 100 balls rose from 4.8 to 5.6; fours stayed near 12.
so what: The extra scoring lines up with more sixes, not more fours. Six-hitting rate is worth tracking when judging batting.

theme: Run scoring is concentrated in a small group
what the data shows: The top 10 batters scored 21% of all runs and the top 50 scored 61%. V Kohli leads with 5,412 runs.
so what: A small group of batters supplies a large share of the runs, so squad planning should protect them.

theme: Strong batters are fast and consistent
what the data shows: 23 of 92 rated batters are 'Strong' on average, strike rate and 30+ starts (best: AD Russell, RR Pant, DA Warner). Lowest rated: PP Chawla, AM Nayar, MS Bisla.
so what: Rate batters on several measures together; total runs alone favours long careers. The lowest group can include bowlers and lower-order batters.

theme: Teams differ in both scoring and defending
what the data shows: Highest scoring side: Chennai Super Kings (153 runs per innings). Best net run difference: Chennai Super Kings (+6.6); weakest: Pune Warriors (-9.8). Teams with 40+ innings only; rain-shortened matches left out.
so what: Team strength shows in runs conceded as much as runs scored. Results are not in the file, so net runs is a proxy.

theme: Batting first scores more, but chasing is not weaker batting
what the data shows: Teams make 154 runs batting first and 143 chasing, because chasers stop at the target.
so what: Compare teams on rates (strike rate, boundaries), not on chasing totals.

theme: Caught is the main way out
what the data shows: 63% of dismissals are caught. Run outs fell from 12.3% of dismissals in 2008 to 6.0% in 2019 (first and last season only; see Objective 3 for the full trend).
so what: Catching is the main route to a wicket, so fielders who take catches matter.

what the data shows: Boundaries per 100 balls and strike rate correlate at r = 0.88 (10+ ball innings). Across seasons, league strike rate tracks sixes per 100 balls at r = 0.93.
so what: Part of this link is built in (boundaries are runs), but boundary frequency is a quick read on how fast a batter scores.

what the data shows: Captains score 26.5 runs per innings against 18.2 for others, but the same batters make 27.3 as captain and 25.2 otherwise. Not-out innings have a strike rate of 148 against 122 for dismissed.
so what: The captain gap is mostly about which batters become captain. Compare captains with themselves, and keep not-out innings separate from dismissed ones.

theme: Exceptional innings are rare and real
what the data shows: 156 innings (1.4%) are 3+ standard deviations above the usual pace for their balls faced; there are 58 hundreds in 11,540 innings.
so what: Big scores are real performances, not errors, so keep them in the data and flag them rather than removing them.
